commit.message:
feat(dfs): Phase 3+4 — solver engine, constraint rules, and optimizer API

- solver.ts: greedy construction + hill-climb + QB×stack diversification,
  all 7 contest modes (CASH/BALANCED/SINGLE_ENTRY/GPP variants/CONTRARIAN/LEVERAGE)
  with calibrated objective weights; dynamic look-ahead budget enforces
  salary cap at every greedy slot without exhausting remaining slots
- rules.ts: 20 rule types — lineup-level (QB_STACK, BRING_BACK, DOUBLE_STACK,
  MAX_PER_TEAM, MAX_FROM_GAME, NO_QB_VS_DST, NO_RB_VS_DST, salary bounds,
  ownership caps, group constraints, conditional locks) and portfolio-level
  EXPOSURE_MIN/MAX; applyRules() + applyPortfolioRules() exports
- POST /api/dfs/optimize: merges salary rows + projections, runs solver,
  persists DfsOptimizerRun + DfsLineupSet + DfsLineup + DfsLineupPlayer
- GET  /api/dfs/optimizer-runs/[id]: full run with nested lineup sets and players
- POST /api/dfs/lineup-sets/[id]/export: DK_CSV and JSON formats
- GET  /api/dfs/lineup-sets/[id]/analytics: portfolio exposure analytics
- 22 tests covering CASH validity, GPP stacking, noQbVsDst, exposure caps

feat(dfs): Phase 5+6 — narrative signal classification and portfolio analytics

- signals.ts: classifyNarrativeImpact() gates every signal through
  hasFootballMechanism(); BIRTHDAY_GAME/REVENGE_GAME → CONTEXT_ONLY (delta=0),
  RETURN_FROM_INJURY → VOLUME, MEDIA_HYPE_SPIKE → HYPE_ONLY; detectHypeInflation()
  flags signals where social velocity exceeds baseline by 3σ; scoreSourceReliability()
  weights by source type, sample size, and recency
- analytics.ts: analyzePortfolio() computes playerExposure, teamExposure,
  chalkConcentration, fragileAssumptionCount; generatePortfolioThesis() and
  generatePortfolioCounterThesis() produce narrative summaries
- GET  /api/dfs/players/[name]/signals: retrieves signals for a player
- POST /api/dfs/signals: creates a new narrative signal for a slate

commit.message:
feat(dfs): Phase 7+8 — lineup thesis generation and Monte Carlo simulation

- lineup-thesis.ts: generateLineupThesis() produces per-lineup narrative
  covering stack evidence + counter-evidence, contest fit, leverage point,
  highest-risk and highest-upside player, late-swap dependencies, and
  whatBreaksThis fragility summary
- engine.ts (simulation): simulate() runs log-normal Monte Carlo (Box-Muller)
  using Float64Array buffers; auto-reduces iterations when lineups×iterations
  exceeds 500k to stay browser-safe; returns p10/p25/p50/p75/p90/p99 per
  lineup plus portfolio-level percentiles and crash probability
- GET /api/dfs/lineups/[id]/thesis: returns thesis for a single lineup
- POST /api/dfs/lineup-sets/[id]/simulate: runs MC and persists DfsSimulationRun
  + DfsSimulationResult rows
- 8 simulation tests covering distribution shape, percentile ordering,
  and auto-reduction

commit.message:
feat(dfs): Phase 9+10 — late-swap engine and post-slate autopsy/calibration

- late-swap/engine.ts: lateSwap() processes lineups after lock; identifies
  scratched players by name, determines the DK slot they fill (QB/RB/WR/TE/DST/FLEX
  via positional count traversal), filters salary-cap-valid replacements,
  sorts preferring same-team-as-QB for stack preservation; produces SwapDecision
  records with whySwap/whyHold text and updated SolvedLineup objects
- POST /api/dfs/lineup-sets/[id]/late-swap: accepts scratchedPlayers + optional
  updatedProjections, runs lateSwap(), persists DfsLateSwapEvent rows
- calibration/autopsy.ts: computeAutopsy() classifies each player result via
  categorize() (GOOD_PROCESS/BAD_PROCESS × GOOD/BAD_OUTCOME + LUCKY/PROJECTION_MISS/
  OWNERSHIP_MISREAD); computes MAE, RMSE, bias, and Pearson-r for both projections
  and ownership; runAutopsy() persists DfsAutopsy + DfsCalibrationResult in a
  single transaction
- POST /api/dfs/slates/[id]/autopsy: validates results, calls runAutopsy(),
  returns calibration metrics + per-player autopsy records
- GET  /api/dfs/slates/[id]/autopsy: retrieves stored autopsies + calibrations

commit.message:
Add OOS split harness and champion/challenger model promoter.

The OOS split harness (oos-split.ts) divides settled picks into in-sample and
out-of-sample cohorts for health assessment. Detects overfit when OOS Brier
significantly exceeds in-sample Brier. Provides segmented health tracking by
pick type/market.

The model promoter (model-promoter.ts) implements safe version progression:
- Champion stays frozen until challenger beats it by a threshold (Brier improvement)
- Challenger must have sufficient OOS sample (CLV proof gate) and healthy OOS metrics
- Never auto-downgrades champion (only promotes or holds)
- Outputs a PromotionDecision that downstream code uses to select model version

Both modules are pure (no I/O); all metrics computed deterministically from
settled pick data. Caller persists promotion decisions and wires the selected
model version into pick generation and receipt minting.

Tests: 14 tests across both modules (7 OOS split, 7 promoter); full test suite
passes (480 tests). Exported from prediction-engine index for use in ingestion
pipeline.

+# GSE Affiliate Program: Compliance Checklist & Quick Reference
+
+**Last Updated**: June 22, 2026  
+**Purpose**: Quick operational checklist for GSE affiliate onboarding, monitoring, and policy enforcement.
+
+---
+
+## Pre-Launch Checklist (Legal & Operational Setup)
+
+### Legal & Contract
+- [ ] Affiliate Agreement drafted with qualified sports/gaming counsel
+- [ ] Agreement includes:
+  - [ ] AGA Responsible Marketing Code compliance clause
+  - [ ] Geo-restriction language (state-by-state allow-list)
+  - [ ] Offshore sportsbook co-promotion ban (explicit, with 150-day termination clause)
+  - [ ] Indemnification clause (affiliate warrants no illegal activity)
+  - [ ] Monitoring & audit rights reserved
+  - [ ] Termination triggers documented (false claims, geo-violation, offshore co-promotion)
+- [ ] Terms reviewed by attorney; ready for signature
+- [ ] Affiliate program Terms of Service published on GSE site
+
+### State Licensing & Regulatory
+- [ ] State licensing guide published (which states require affiliate licensing, fees, application steps)
+- [ ] Affiliate onboarding form includes affidavit: "I have reviewed state licensing requirements for my jurisdiction(s)"
+- [ ] Affiliate dashboard flags licensing requirements for their target states
+- [ ] Disclaimer added: "GSE does not provide legal advice; affiliates responsible for state licensing compliance"
+
+### Brand & Marketing Standards
+- [ ] Approved promotional language examples published (showing AGA-compliant phrasing)
+- [ ] Banned phrase list published (no "risk-free," "guaranteed," etc.)
+- [ ] Responsible gaming messaging template provided (NCPG link, "past performance" disclaimer)
+- [ ] Logo/brand guidelines confirm 21+ targeting only
+- [ ] Social media content guidelines include geo-targeting restrictions
+
+### Technical Setup
+- [ ] Affiliate referral links include geo-blocking (no traffic from prohibited states)
+- [ ] Geo-blocking tested on at least 5 prohibited states (Arizona IP, California IP, etc.)
+- [ ] Affiliate dashboard displays state restrictions for each partner (DraftKings, FanDuel)
+- [ ] Monitoring system configured: daily scan of affiliate websites/social for banned phrases
+- [ ] Termination workflow documented (legal notice, 10-day cure period, then account suspension)
+
+### Operator Coordination
+- [ ] DraftKings Affiliate Program Terms reviewed; compliance mapped
+- [ ] FanDuel Affiliate Program Terms reviewed; compliance mapped
+- [ ] Written communication sent to both: GSE is affiliate promotional hub; confirm compliance expectations
+- [ ] Quarterly compliance reporting plan established
+
+---
+
+## Affiliate Onboarding Checklist
+
+### For Every New Affiliate:
+1. **Before Approval**
+   - [ ] Affiliate completes onboarding form (affidavit on state licensing, no offshore co-promotion)
+   - [ ] Affiliate confirms they are 21+ and legal US resident (or Ontario resident)
+   - [ ] Target states provided; GSE maps to allowed states for DraftKings, FanDuel
+   - [ ] Affiliate T&C signature collected
+   - [ ] Affiliate completes AGA Code training (or attestation they've read it)
+
+2. **Approval**
+   - [ ] Affiliate account activated
+   - [ ] Personalized state restriction list emailed (e.g., "Your traffic must come from: AZ, CO, CT, IL, IN...")
+   - [ ] Approved promotional materials (templates, sample posts) provided
+   - [ ] Affiliate dashboard walkthrough (geo-restrictions, RG messaging, banned phrases)
+   - [ ] Support contact info provided (compliance@gse.com)
+
+3. **First 30 Days (Monitoring)**
+   - [ ] Affiliate's website/social media audited manually (banned phrases scan)
+   - [ ] Referral traffic spot-checked (geo-blocking verification; are clicks coming only from legal states?)
+   - [ ] Performance metrics reviewed (unusual patterns flagged)
+   - [ ] Affiliate sent reminder: compliance expectations, reporting mechanism for questions
+
+---
+
+## Ongoing Monitoring Checklist (Monthly/Quarterly)
+
+### Monthly (Automated + Spot-Check)
+- [ ] **Traffic Audit**: Sample 50 affiliates; verify referral traffic originates only from allowed states
+  - Tool: IP geolocation on referral source check
+  - Violation: Refer to legal for potential termination
+- [ ] **Phrase Scan**: Automated scan of affiliate promotional content for banned phrases
+  - Monitor: Affiliate websites, social posts (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram)
+  - Flag: Any "risk-free," "guarantee," "lock," "sure bet" language
+  - Action: Email affiliate within 48 hours; require correction within 5 business days
+- [ ] **RG Messaging Check**: Spot-check 25 affiliates; confirm NCPG link and "past performance" disclaimer present
+  - Violation: Request correction; document in audit log
+- [ ] **Offshore Co-Promotion Scan**: Search affiliate domain + "offshore" or "Bovada" or known offshore books
+  - Violation: Immediate escalation; legal review for termination
+
+### Quarterly (Strategic Review)
+- [ ] State licensing requirement changes? (Subscribe to state gaming commission alerts)
+  - Update affiliate guide; notify all affiliates in affected states
+- [ ] AGA Code updates? (Subscribe to AGA website)
+  - Review changes; update affiliate training materials
+- [ ] Operator (DraftKings/FanDuel) terms changes?
+  - Map changes to GSE compliance; communicate to affiliates
+- [ ] Affiliate complaints/escalations review
+  - Are there patterns? (e.g., repeated geo-blocking failures in one state = investigation)
+- [ ] Compliance metrics report
+  - Total active affiliates / affiliates terminated for cause / violations flagged
+  - Share with DraftKings, FanDuel, GSE leadership
+
+### Annually
+- [ ] Legal review of affiliate agreement (are we capturing new regulations?)
+- [ ] Affiliate education webinar (AGA Code, state updates, case studies)
+- [ ] Affiliate survey (what are their compliance pain points? Gaps in guidance?)
+
+---
+
+## Affiliate Violation Response Flowchart
+
+```
+VIOLATION DETECTED (geo-blocking, banned phrase, offshore co-promotion, etc.)
+
+    ↓
+    
+1. SEVERITY ASSESS
+   ├─ 🔴 CRITICAL (offshore co-promo, offshore traffic, targeting minors, repeated geo-violations)
+   │  └─ → IMMEDIATE: Legal review for termination
+   │     → Send 7-day cure notice (optional; operator discretion)
+   │     → If not cured, terminate account + flag for operator notification
+   │
+   └─ 🟠 MODERATE (single geo-violation, banned phrase, missing RG link, single-incident pattern)
+      └─ → 48-hour notice to affiliate
+         → 5-business-day cure period
+         → Escalate if not cured
+
+    ↓
+
+2. NOTICE SENT
+   ├─ Document violation (screenshot, URL, timestamp)
+   ├─ Email affiliate with:
+   │  ├─ Violation description + evidence
+   │  ├─ Requirement & policy reference (AGA Code, GSE T&Cs, state law)
+   │  ├─ Cure deadline & remediation steps
+   │  ├─ Escalation warning (repeated violations = termination)
+   │
+   └─ Log in Compliance Audit Trail
+
+    ↓
+
+3. CURE PERIOD
+   ├─ Affiliate has 5 business days (or 7 days for critical) to respond/cure
+   ├─ GSE follows up mid-period (friendly check-in)
+   ├─ If affiliate responds with questions, support@compliance provides guidance
+   └─ If no response by deadline → escalate to legal
+
+    ↓
+
+4. OUTCOME
+   ├─ ✅ CURED: Affiliate corrects issue; account remains active; incident logged
+   ├─ ⚠️ PARTIAL CURE: Issue partially addressed; re-audit required; warnings escalated
+   └─ ❌ NOT CURED: Escalate to legal; prepare termination notice (10-day final notice recommended)
+      └─ If terminated: operator notified; account suspended; compliance report updated
+
+    ↓
+
+5. TERMINATION (If Necessary)
+   ├─ Final 10-day notice sent (email + certified mail)
+   ├─ Affiliate given last chance to respond
+   ├─ If no cure, account suspended + affiliate removed from dashboard
+   ├─ Operator notification sent (DraftKings, FanDuel)
+   ├─ Incident documented in audit trail
+   └─ Compliance report updated
+
+```
+
+---
+
+## Common Compliance Violations & Remediation
+
+| Violation | Severity | Cure | Policy Ref |
+|-----------|----------|------|-----------|
+| **Geo-violation**: Traffic from prohibited state (UT, HI, WA, etc.) | 🔴 CRITICAL | Geo-blocking fix + revert traffic 30 days; audit affiliate's ad settings | State law; GSE T&Cs |
+| **Banned phrase**: "Risk-free bet," "guaranteed," "lock" | 🟠 MODERATE | Remove all instances within 5 business days; attestation that copy updated | AGA Code (March 2023) |
+| **Missing RG messaging**: NCPG link not visible in ads/site | 🟠 MODERATE | Add NCPG link + "past performance disclaimer" within 5 days | AGA Code; GSE Affiliate T&Cs |
+| **Offshore co-promotion**: Website promotes Bovada, BetOnline, etc. alongside DraftKings/FanDuel | 🔴 CRITICAL | Immediate removal; written attestation that offshore book removed; 150-day window to terminate one or the other | FanDuel T&Cs; GSE Affiliate Clause |
+| **False performance claims**: "90% win rate," "beat the book guaranteed" | 🔴 CRITICAL | Immediate removal; written attestation; legal review for termination | AGA Code; FTC Act; State UDAPs |
+| **Targeting minors**: Content on college campuses, TikTok ads without 21+ gate, etc. | 🔴 CRITICAL | Immediate review & removal; escalate to legal | AGA Code; state ad law |
+| **Promoting to prohibited state**: Running ads in California (where sportsbook illegal) | 🔴 CRITICAL | Cease ad campaigns; geo-restrict ads to legal states; audit account for other violations | State law; operator T&Cs |
+| **Missing state licensing disclaimer**: Affiliate in state requiring licensing but no mention | 🟠 MODERATE | Add disclaimer: "Affiliate has obtained required state license(s) as of [date]" | State law; GSE guidance |
+
+---
+
+## Affiliate Termination Letter Template
+
+```
+Subject: NOTICE OF TERMINATION — [Affiliate Name] GSE Affiliate Program
+
+Dear [Affiliate Name],
+
+Effective [date + 10 business days], your participation in the GSE Affiliate Program is TERMINATED due to material breach of the Affiliate Agreement dated [date].
+
+REASON FOR TERMINATION:
+[Specific violation, with dates/evidence]
+
+EXAMPLES:
+- Promotion of offshore gambling sites (Bovada, BetOnline) alongside DraftKings/FanDuel (prohibited under Affiliate Agreement Section 4.2)
+- Use of banned marketing language ("risk-free bet") on [website URL] dated [date] (prohibited under AGA Responsible Marketing Code)
+- Geo-violation: Promotional traffic sourced from Utah (prohibited state) on [date] (prohibited under Affiliate Agreement Section 3.1)
+
+REQUIRED ACTIONS (by [date]):
+1. Cease all promotion of GSE, DraftKings, and FanDuel within 48 hours
+2. Remove all GSE/DraftKings/FanDuel promotional content from your website and social media within 5 business days
+3. Return all promotional materials and logos
+4. Provide written attestation that all prohibited activity has ceased (offshore co-promotion, banned language, etc.)
+
+ACCOUNT STATUS:
+- Your affiliate dashboard is suspended as of [date]
+- All pending commissions through [date] will be paid per original schedule (if applicable)
+- Future commission payments are withheld pending completion of required actions
+
+APPEALS:
+If you believe this termination is in error, you may submit a written appeal to compliance@gse.com within 10 business days, including:
+- Explanation of cure/corrective action taken
+- Evidence that violation has been resolved
+- Request for account reinstatement review
+
+Your appeal will be reviewed by GSE legal within 10 business days.
+
+REGULATORY NOTIFICATION:
+GSE is required to notify DraftKings Affiliate Program and FanDuel Affiliate Program of this termination per our Operating Agreements. This may impact your suitability for future affiliate participation with these operators.
+
+If you have questions, contact compliance@gse.com.
+
+Regards,
+[GSE Compliance Team]
+
+cc: Legal; Operators (DraftKings, FanDuel)
+```
+
+---
+
+## State Licensing Quick Reference (Affiliate Onboarding)
+
+When affiliates ask, "Do I need a license?", use this matrix:

+### Commission Structures
+- **DraftKings**: 25%–40% RevShare; $100–$600 CPA (state-dependent)

+## Executive Summary
+
+- **Geographic Reach**: Affiliate programs for DraftKings and FanDuel are restricted to **38+ US states** + **Ontario, Canada**. No operations in EU/UK/Asia/Australia.
+- **Licensing Reality**: Licensing is **mandatory in some states** (Arizona, Colorado, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania) and **optional/absent in others** (Iowa). Fees range from **free (NJ) to $2,500+ (PA, Michigan)**.
+- **DFS vs. Sportsbook Affiliate Distinction**: DFS affiliates face minimal/no licensing in most states; sportsbook affiliates face state-by-state licensing requirements.
+- **Compliance Floor**: AGA Responsible Marketing Code (March 2023 update) applies to all affiliates; no "risk-free" claims, 21+ targeting only, responsible gaming messaging mandatory.
+- **Offshore Ban**: FanDuel and DraftKings explicitly ban affiliates from co-promoting offshore sportsbooks—violation triggers program termination and blocks future regulatory licensing.

+### 3.1 AGA Responsible Marketing Code (Applies to All Affiliates)

+**Effective Date**: March 2023 (most recent update)  
+**Scope**: Binds all affiliates and agents of AGA member operators.

+**Key Prohibitions:**
+- ❌ "Risk-free" bet language (banned March 2023)
+- ❌ "Guaranteed wins" or similar certainty claims
+- ❌ Targeting college-aged populations; no partnerships promoting wagering to colleges
+- ❌ Targeting audiences under 21 in advertising
+- ❌ False or misleading win-rate/performance claims without historical data
+
+**Mandatory Requirements:**
+- ✅ Responsible gaming helpline link (NCPG 1-800-GAMBLER) in all promotional materials
+- ✅ Clear age verification (21+) in all affiliate materials
+- ✅ Disclosure of terms and conditions in advertising
+- ✅ Internal review process for affiliate marketing
+- ✅ Training provision to affiliates on Code compliance
+
+**Affiliate-Specific Obligations (AGA Code):**
+1. Operators must distribute the Code to all third-party partners (affiliates, agencies, media buyers)
+2. Operators must implement contractual compliance requirements in affiliate agreements
+3. Affiliates must warrant compliance with AGA Code in their agreements
+4. Monitoring and audit rights are contractually enforceable
+
+**Enforcement:**
+- Code Compliance Review Board (CCRB): 2 independent co-chairs + 5 AGA member reps (3-year terms)
+- Self-regulatory (industry), not government-enforced, but violations can trigger regulatory penalties

+**Reference**: [AGA Responsible Marketing Code Updates](https://www.americangaming.org/new-updates-to-aga-responsible-marketing-code-for-sports-wagering-prohibit-risk-free-enhance-college-aged-protections/)

+# Research Summary: DFS Sportsbook Affiliate Geographic Restrictions & Compliance (2024-2025)
+
+**Research Date**: June 22, 2026  
+**Researcher**: Claude Code Agent  
+**Scope**: DraftKings, FanDuel, and major DFS sportsbook affiliate program availability, licensing, state restrictions, international operations, and compliance requirements  
+**Status**: Complete
+
+---
+
+## Research Objectives Completed
+
+✅ Map which US states allow affiliate promotions for DFS sportsbooks  
+✅ Identify international restrictions on DraftKings/FanDuel affiliate programs  
+✅ Document state-by-state licensing requirements and fees  
+✅ Research AGA Responsible Marketing Code compliance requirements  
+✅ Find official T&Cs and regulatory compliance checkpoints  
+✅ Compile action items for GSE affiliate program launch  
+
+---
+
+## Key Findings Summary
+
+### Geographic Availability
+
+**North America Only**:
+- DraftKings and FanDuel affiliate programs operate in **38 US states + Ontario, Canada** (sportsbook only)
+- **No international expansion**: UK, EU, Australia, Asia — all unavailable for affiliate programs
+- **Ontario DFS Discontinued**: Both operators discontinued DFS in Ontario citing regulatory constraints (contests limited to in-province participants only)
+
+**Prohibited States** (12):
+Alaska, Alabama, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Mississippi, Nevada, New Mexico, South Dakota, Utah (constitutional ban), Washington
+
+---
+
+### State-by-State Affiliate Licensing
+
+**Free Licensing**:
+- New Jersey (vendor registration; operator must submit on affiliate's behalf)
+
+**Low-Cost ($200–$500)**:
+- Colorado ($350 for CPA basis)
+- Indiana ($500)
+- Michigan ($200 for CPA)
+- Tennessee ($500, reported)
+- Virginia ($500, reported)
+
+**Medium-Cost ($1,000–$1,500)**:
+- Arizona ($1,500 initial + $500 renewal)
+- West Virginia ($1,000)
+
+**High-Cost ($2,000+)**:
+- New Jersey RevShare ($2,000)
+- Michigan RevShare ($2,500–$5,000 + $5,000 annual)
+- Pennsylvania ($2,500+)
+
+**No State Licensing Required**:
+- Iowa (no state requirement for marketing affiliates)
+
+**States with Limited/Unclear Guidance**:
+Most states do not publish detailed affiliate licensing requirements; affiliates must contact state gaming commissions directly.
+
+---
+
+### AGA Responsible Marketing Code Compliance (March 2023 Update)
+
+**Mandatory Requirements** (all affiliates):
+- ❌ No "risk-free," "guarantee," "lock," or similar certainty claims
+- ✅ 21+ targeting only; no college partnerships or minor targeting
+- ✅ NCPG helpline link (1-800-GAMBLER) in all promotional materials
+- ✅ Disclosure of terms and wagering requirements
+- ✅ Responsible gaming messaging ("past performance ≠ future results")
+- ✅ Internal compliance review process (operator responsibility)
+- ✅ Training and distribution of Code to affiliates and agents
+
+**Enforcement**:
+- Self-regulated by AGA Code Compliance Review Board (2 independent co-chairs + 5 AGA member reps)
+- Violations can trigger state regulatory penalties; operators hold affiliates accountable via contract
+
+---
+
+### Offshore Sportsbook Ban (Critical Finding)
+
+**FanDuel Position** (Strictest):
+- Explicit 150-day notice to cease co-promoting offshore sportsbooks OR cease FanDuel affiliation
+- Failure to comply triggers:
+  - Immediate termination
+  - Regulatory coordination with state gaming commissions
+  - **Affiliate flagged as unsuitable for future state gaming licenses**
+- Language in T&Cs: "By participating in FanDuel Affiliate Program, you warrant your site does not promote illegal activities including offshore gambling"
+
+**DraftKings Position** (Strict):
+- Cannot co-promote DraftKings alongside unlicensed/offshore sportsbooks
+- Termination + regulatory impact if breach detected
+- Less explicit than FanDuel but same outcome
+
+**Implication for GSE Affiliates**:
+- GSE must explicitly prohibit offshore co-promotion in affiliate agreement
+- Breach must result in immediate termination + operator notification
+- Affiliate suitability for future gaming licenses at stake
+
+---
+
+### Commission Structures
+
+**DraftKings**:
+- RevShare: 25%–40% of net gaming revenue (higher rates first 30 days)
+- CPA: $100–$600 per acquisition (state/vertical-dependent)
+- Attribution window: 30 days
+- Min payout threshold: $50
+
+**FanDuel**:
+- CPA: $25–$35+ (tiered by volume)
+- RevShare: Flat 35% (no tiering)
+- Attribution window: 30 days
+- Min payout threshold: ~$50
+
+---
+
+### International Restrictions
+
+| Region | DraftKings | FanDuel | Status |
+|--------|---|---|---|
+| **UK** | No affiliate program | No affiliate program | Not available |
+| **EU** | No affiliate program | No affiliate program | Not available |
+| **Australia** | No affiliate program | No affiliate program | Not available |
+| **Asia** | No affiliate program | No affiliate program | Not available |
+| **Canada (non-Ontario)** | Blocked | Blocked | Not available |
+| **Ontario** | Sportsbook only (DFS discontinued) | Sportsbook only (DFS discontinued) | Limited availability |
+
+**Finding**: Zero international expansion of affiliate programs as of 2026. North America focus only.
+
+---
+
+### DFS vs. Sportsbook Affiliate Distinction
+
+| Factor | DFS Affiliates | Sportsbook Affiliates |
+|--------|---|---|
+| **Federal Classification** | Skill-based (UIGEA exempt) | Gambling (state-regulated) |
+| **Licensing Required** | Minimal/None in most states | Required in most regulated states |
+| **Restricted States** | 6 (WA, ID, MT, NV, HI, OR) | 12 (+ CA, TX where DFS legal) |
+| **Age Requirement** | 18+ (varies: some 19 or 21) | 21+ (standard) |
+
+**Opportunity**: Affiliates can operate DFS in California, Texas, Florida (no sportsbook) where sportsbooks are prohibited. Geographic arbitrage exists.
+
+---
+
+### Compliance Checkpoints for GSE
+
+**Critical Gaps** (must address before affiliate program launch):
+1. ❌ Affiliate agreement incorporating AGA Code compliance language
+2. ❌ State licensing guide + affiliate attestation
+3. ❌ Offshore sportsbook ban clause + monitoring
+4. ❌ Marketing audit SOP (banned phrase scanner + geo-blocking verification)
+5. ❌ Affiliate termination protocol (documentation + operator notification)

+**Recommended Actions** (in priority order):

+3. Implement geo-blocking verification on affiliate referral links
+4. Set up automated content scanner for banned phrases + offshore keywords

+/**
+ * Prediction methodology data contract for Galaxy Sports Edge.
+ * Documents Vegas mechanics, calibration science, statistical methods,
+ * and the GSE No-Play doctrine.
+ *
+ * Sources: public academic literature, industry standard definitions.
+ * Do not fabricate performance claims or user outcomes.
+ */
+
+// ── Core methodology types ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+export type CalibrationMetricId =
+  | "mae"
+  | "rmse"
+  | "brier_score"
+  | "log_loss"
+  | "pearson_r"
+  | "clv"
+  | "roi"
+  | "win_rate"
+  | "ev_per_bet"
+  | "closing_line_value"
+  | "overround";
+
+export type StatMethodId =
+  | "linear_regression"
+  | "logistic_regression"
+  | "gradient_boosting"
+  | "random_forest"
+  | "neural_network"
+  | "poisson_regression"
+  | "bayesian_updating"
+  | "monte_carlo"
+  | "kelly_criterion"
+  | "elo_rating"
+  | "ensemble";
+
+export type SignalType =
+  | "opening_line"
+  | "closing_line"
+  | "reverse_line_movement"
+  | "steam_move"
+  | "public_money_percentage"
+  | "sharp_money_percentage"
+  | "weather"
+  | "injury"
+  | "line_freeze"
+  | "off_market_price";
+
+export type NoPlayReason =
+  | "signal_conflict"
+  | "low_confidence"
+  | "line_moved_against"
+  | "injury_uncertainty"
+  | "weather_extreme"
+  | "correlated_exposure"
+  | "market_efficient"
+  | "insufficient_data";
+
+export interface CalibrationMetric {
+  id: CalibrationMetricId;
+  name: string;
+  formula: string;
+  interpretation: string;
+  goodRange: string;
+  gseUsage: string;
+}
+

+  id: StatMethodId;
+  name: string;
+  useCase: string;
+  strengths: string[];

+  gseApplication: string;
+}

+  id: string;
+  name: string;
+  explanation: string;
+  formulaOrExample: string;
+  gseSignalValue: string;
+}
+
+export interface SignalDefinition {
+  type: SignalType;
+  name: string;
+  description: string;

+  gseWeight: "primary" | "secondary" | "contextual";

+  label: string;
+  triggerConditions: string[];
+  displayText: string;
+  suppressionBehavior: "hide_pick" | "show_watchlist" | "show_no_play_card";
+}
+
+// ── Calibration metrics ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+export const CALIBRATION_METRICS: ReadonlyArray<CalibrationMetric> = [
+  {
+    id: "mae",
+    name: "Mean Absolute Error",
+    formula: "MAE = mean(|actual − predicted|)",
+    interpretation:
+      "Average magnitude of error. Lower is better. Treats all errors equally regardless of direction.",
+    goodRange: "Fantasy points: < 4 pts. Ownership: < 5pp.",
+    gseUsage: "Primary autopsy metric; tracked per slate, per model version.",
+  },
+  {
+    id: "rmse",
+    name: "Root Mean Square Error",
+    formula: "RMSE = sqrt(mean((actual − predicted)²))",
+    interpretation:
+      "Penalizes large errors more than MAE. Use alongside MAE; large RMSE vs MAE gap signals outlier misses.",
+    goodRange: "Fantasy points: < 6 pts.",
+    gseUsage: "Secondary autopsy metric. RMSE/MAE ratio used to detect tail-risk issues.",
+  },
+  {
+    id: "brier_score",
+    name: "Brier Score",
+    formula: "BS = mean((probability − outcome)²)",
+    interpretation:
+      "0 = perfect, 1 = perfectly wrong. Standard for probability calibration. Lower is better.",
+    goodRange: "< 0.20 for game outcomes; random = 0.25.",
+    gseUsage:
+      "Used for binary outcomes (cover spread, win/loss). Enables calibration curve plotting.",
+  },
+  {
+    id: "log_loss",
+    name: "Log Loss (Cross-Entropy)",
+    formula: "LogLoss = −mean(y·log(p) + (1−y)·log(1−p))",
+    interpretation:
+      "Heavily penalizes confident wrong predictions. Complement to Brier score; more sensitive to probability quality.",
+    goodRange: "< 0.50 for spread outcomes.",
+    gseUsage: "Secondary probability quality metric; used in ensemble model selection.",
+  },
+  {
+    id: "pearson_r",
+    name: "Pearson Correlation",
+    formula: "r = cov(X,Y) / (σX · σY)",
+    interpretation:

+// Typed registry entry
+export interface FooEntry {
+  readonly id: string;
+  readonly name: string;
+  // ... fields with no `any`
+}
+
+// Registry as ReadonlyArray — use `as const` on inner objects
+export const FOO_REGISTRY: ReadonlyArray<FooEntry> = [
+  { id: "example", name: "Example", /* ... */ },

+

+export function filteredFoo(entries: ReadonlyArray<FooEntry>): ReadonlyArray<FooEntry> {

+# IDP Scoring Data Sources Research Report
+
+**Date:** 2026-06-22  
+**Scope:** Individual Defensive Player (IDP) scoring, snap counts, play-by-play data, and defensive statistics  
+**Status:** Comprehensive market research for platform integration
+
+---
+
+## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
+
+Galaxy Sports Edge currently ingests odds data via The Odds API and historical schedules from nflverse. Expanding to IDP scoring, snap counts, and defensive statistics requires evaluating sources across three dimensions:
+
+1. **Data Coverage:** Temporal range, granularity (season/week/game), and player population
+2. **Update Frequency:** Real-time, daily, weekly, or historical-only
+3. **Licensing & Legal Posture:** Commercial-use permission, attribution requirements, ToS compliance
+
+**Key Finding:** The nflverse project (CC-BY-4.0 licensed, open-data) already provides comprehensive snap counts and play-by-play data back to 1999 for free. No additional vendor is required for historical IDP scoring or snap-count baseline data. Premium vendors (PFF, Sportradar, SportsDataIO) are needed only for proprietary grades, real-time updates, or advanced metrics.
+
+---
+
+## 1. AVAILABLE SOURCES — DETAILED ANALYSIS
+
+### TIER 1: OPEN DATA (Free, Commercial-Use Approved)
+
+#### **1.1 nflverse (nflverse-data)**
+
+**URL:** https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data  
+**License:** CC-BY-4.0 (data); MIT (tooling)  
+**Commercial Use:** ✅ Permitted (with attribution required)
+
+**Data Coverage:**
+
+| Dataset | Coverage | Grain | Freshness |
+|---------|----------|-------|-----------|
+| **snap_counts** | 2012–present | Player-game-position | Weekly (postseason) |
+| **pbp (play-by-play)** | 1999–present | Play-level | Weekly release, historical |
+| **pfr_advstats** | 2018–present | Player-week | Weekly |
+| **ngs (Next Gen Stats)** | 2016–present | Player-week | Weekly |
+| **player_stats_week** | 1999–present | Player-week (offensive) | Weekly |
+| **depth_charts** | 2001–present | Player-week | Weekly |
+| **pbp_participation** | 2016–present | Play-level | Weekly (CC-BY-SA-4.0 variant) |
+| **ftn_charting** | 2022–present | Play-level | Weekly (manual charting) |
+
+**What It Provides for IDP:**
+
+- **Snap Counts:** Full offense/defense/ST snap counts per player-game (e.g., "DE snaps," "LB snaps")
+- **Play-by-Play:** Tackling assignments (implicit via play charting), sack credit, pressure, pass deflection
+- **Advanced Defense Stats:** Via `pfr_advstats` — tackles, sacks, FF, etc. (available from 2018)
+- **Next Gen Stats:** Defensive separation, cushion, time-to-throw, acceleration for pass-rushers
+- **Participation Data:** Personnel groupings per play (who was on field per snap) — useful for role context
+
+**Update Frequency:** Weekly release (postseason); typically available ~48 hours after game  
+**Historical Depth:** Snap counts back to 2012; play-by-play back to 1999  
+**Rate Limits:** None (bulk download from GitHub releases)  
+**Attribution Required:** Yes — "Data via nflverse (nflverse-data), licensed CC BY 4.0"  
+**Integration Effort:** Low (already used for scheduling; same infrastructure)
+
+**Licensing Note:** Most datasets are CC-BY-4.0. Exceptions: `pbp_participation` and `ftn_charting` are CC-BY-SA-4.0 (share-alike), so derivative works must be licensed identically. Safe to ingest both but keep licensing flag separate in schema.
+
+**Verdict for GSE:** ✅ **PRIMARY SOURCE for historical IDP baseline.** All snap counts, play-by-play, advanced stats, and Next Gen data are legally available for commercial use with attribution. No cost, no vendor relationship risk.

+# Fantasy Football League Data Sources & APIs Research Report
+**Date:** June 22, 2026  
+**Compiled by:** Claude Code Research Agent
+
+---
+
+## Executive Summary
+
+Three primary fantasy football platforms provide league data access via APIs: **Sleeper**, **Yahoo Fantasy Sports**, and **ESPN Fantasy**. Additionally, **MyFantasyLeague (MFL)** offers a paid developer API. Each has distinct authentication models, data availability, rate limits, and technical requirements for league benchmarking.
+
+---
+
+## 1. SLEEPER API
+
+### Overview
+- **Status:** Fully operational, free tier only
+- **Authentication:** None required (public read-only API)
+- **Cost:** Free
+- **Best for:** Quick prototyping, public league data, no authentication overhead
+
+### League Data Access
+**Available Endpoints:**
+- `GET /v1/league/<league_id>` - League metadata
+- `GET /v1/league/<league_id>/rosters` - All rosters in league
+- `GET /v1/league/<league_id>/users` - All users/owners in league
+- `GET /v1/league/<league_id>/matchups?round=<week>` - Weekly matchup data
+- `GET /v1/players/nfl` - Full NFL player map (~14MB)
+- `GET /v1/players/nfl/trending/{add|drop}?lookback_hours=X&limit=Y` - Market momentum
+
+**League-Level Metrics Available:**
+- League size (number of rosters/owners)
+- Roster positions
+- League status
+- Season year
+- Individual roster records (wins, losses, ties)
+- Points for (PF)
+- Points for decimal precision
+- Win-loss-tie records per roster
+- Matchup results by week
+- Starter vs. bench roster composition
+
+### Rate Limits
+**Conflicting documentation sources; recommendations:**
+- Conservative: 90 requests per minute per IP
+- Aggressive: 1000 calls per minute (stated in some community sources)
+- **Recommendation:** Stay under 90 req/min to avoid IP blocking; monitor for 429 responses
+
+### Authentication Model
+- No API keys or tokens required
+- Public access to all league data
+- No OAuth flow needed
+- IP-based rate limiting only
+
+### Code Example (from codebase)
+Located in `/apps/web/lib/integrations/sleeper.ts`:
+- Pure normalizers for User, League, Roster
+- Read-only sync (never writes to league)
+- Fetches rosters, players, and trending data
+- Caches the 14MB player map (6-hour TTL) to avoid redundant fetches
+
+---
+
+## 2. YAHOO FANTASY SPORTS API
+
+### Overview
+- **Status:** Requires OAuth 2.0 approval
+- **Authentication:** OAuth 2.0
+- **Cost:** Free with approval
+- **Best for:** Official, long-term integrations; user-specific data; multi-sport support
+
+### League Data Access
+**Supported Sports:**
+- Football (NFL)
+- Baseball (MLB)
+- Basketball (NBA)
+- Hockey (NHL)
+
+**Authentication Requirements:**
+1. Request API access via Yahoo Developer Portal
+2. Accept API Access and Use Agreement
+3. Submit organization, product, and use-case information
+4. Receive OAuth 2.0 credentials (Client ID & Secret)
+
+**Available Data:**
+- Games
+- League information
+- Team rosters
+- Player statistics
+- Matchups
+- Transactions (waiver claims, trades, free agent pickups)
+- Final standings
+
+**League-Level Metrics Available:**
+- League metadata (scoring format, settings)

+- Points for/against per team
+- Head-to-head matchup results
+- Transaction history (trades, waivers, pickups)
+- Player ownership across league
+- Bench vs. active roster info
+- League-wide scoring trends
+
+### Rate Limits
+- Subject to standard OAuth rate limiting
+- Documentation does not specify explicit limits
+- Appears to be lenient for approved developers
+
+### Important Notes
+- Private leagues: Only members can access data
+- Requires user authentication and consent
+- Supports historical data across multiple seasons
+- FAAB (Free Agent Acquisition Budget) data may not be directly available
+
+### Access Process
+1. Visit [Yahoo Developer Portal](https://developer.yahoo.com/fantasysports/guide/)
+2. Review API documentation
+3. Submit access request with business justification
+4. Wait for approval (typically 5-10 business days)
+5. Implement OAuth 2.0 flow
+
+---

+## 3. ESPN FANTASY API
+
+### Overview
+- **Status:** Unofficial / Undocumented
+- **Authentication:** Session-based (require cookies)
+- **Cost:** Free
+- **Best for:** Private league data scraping; no approval needed; rapid integration
+
+### League Data Access
+**Important Limitations:**
+- No official public API
+- Access via undocumented hidden endpoints
+- Requires direct browser authentication
+- As of August 2025, ESPN restricted historical data access
+
+**Authentication Method:**
+1. Log into ESPN.com via web browser
+2. Copy two cookies from DevTools:
+   - `espn_s2` - Session token

+3. Pass cookies with API requests
+
+**Available Data:**

+- All team rosters
+- Matchup results by week
+- Player statistics
+- League standings
+- Transaction history (limited)

+**League-Level Metrics Available:**

+export function runFuturesSimulation(
+  board: DraftBoard,
+  picksUntilNext: number,
+  adpRecords: AdpRecord[],
+  simulationCount?: number  // default 500
+): FuturesTree
+```
+
+Algorithm for `runFuturesSimulation`:
+1. For each simulation, for each pick between now and user's next turn:
+   - Compute pick probability for each available player using ADP as weight (player with ADP closest to current pick number has highest probability)
+   - Sample one player using weighted random
+   - Remove from available pool
+2. After all simulations, for each player, compute fraction of simulations where player was not taken = returnProbability

+## SAFETY GATES
+
+These are hard stops — not guidelines. Enforce them in every phase.
+
+### Data label enforcement
+
+Every piece of player/projection data must carry `DataLabel`:
+- `'ILLUSTRATIVE'` — synthetic/demo data, clearly labeled as example
+- `'MODELED'` — computed by GSE model, not from licensed source
+- `'LICENSED'` — from a licensed, contracted data provider
+
+Do not present MODELED data as if it were LICENSED. Every UI component that displays projections must show the badge.
+
+### No real player projections without license
+
+Until a projection data source contract is signed (owner action item), all player projected point values must be:
+1. Labeled `'MODELED'` or `'ILLUSTRATIVE'`
+2. Marked with a visible disclaimer in the UI
+3. Not referenced in any marketing copy as "real projections"
+
+### No Voice Jarvis response that claims guaranteed outcome
+
+The Jarvis system prompt must include: "You are an advisory assistant only. Do not guarantee any outcome. Do not say 'you should take' — say 'the recommendation is.' Do not say 'this will win you the league' — say 'this improves your expected points.' Under no circumstances suggest auto-drafting."
+
+### No auto-drafting
+
+No code path should ever submit a pick on the user's behalf without explicit user action (click or confirmed voice command with confirmation step). Auto-draft is not a feature — it is a liability.
+
+### No live platform sync without ToS approval
+
+Do not write any code that reads draft state from Yahoo/ESPN/Sleeper live feeds. If user asks for this, return: "Live sync requires platform ToS review — coming soon."
+

+## ANTI-PATTERNS TO AVOID
+
+1. Do not add `any` types. TypeScript strict mode is enforced. If a type is genuinely unknown, use `unknown` and narrow it.
+2. Do not skip tests. No phase is complete without passing tests.
+3. Do not modify DFS optimizer files. They are done. Leave them alone.
+4. Do not modify Stripe/auth/entitlement infrastructure. They are live.
+5. Do not create new color definitions — use existing design tokens.
+6. Do not fabricate player data. Use clearly-labeled illustrative fixtures.
+7. Do not call the Scraping Clearance Engine with any fantasy source that isn't in the source-rights-registry. If unsure, do not scrape.
+8. Do not build evasion tooling (CAPTCHA bypass, credential misuse, proxy rotation). These are permanently excluded per CLAUDE.md.
+9. Do not build the Chrome extension or live OAuth sync — these are founder-gated.
+10. Do not present uncertainty as certainty. Every recommendation must include what makes it wrong.
